intro_bio: Hi, I’m Romeo De Timmerman, a researcher at Ghent University combining computational and sociolinguistic approaches to study language variation.

bio: I am a doctoral researcher in Linguistics at Ghent University, where I also obtained master's degrees in Linguistics and Statistical Data Analysis. My current research primarily focuses on how well large language models handle linguistically varied input. I will soon join the Department of Computer Science at Columbia University as a postdoctoral researcher, funded by the Belgian American Educational Foundation and the Commission for Educational Exchange between the United States, Belgium and Luxembourg.

project_items.description: Evaluating how well Large Language Models (LLMs) handle African American English (AAE) input. The project focuses on two tasks: feature classification and next turn generation. The evaluation dataset comprises authentic dialogue excerpts from CORAAL.

Modeling formant trajectories of PRICE vowels using feature engineering, dimensionality reduction, gradient boosted decision trees, and neural networks. This project applies interpretable machine learning to explore gradient vowel production and categorical perception.

Predicting the presence of African American English features in blues singing using gradient boosted decision trees. This project combines machine learning and sociolinguistics to examine patterns of linguistic variation in musical performance.
